title: The Nassau-Wetterau theologians at Dort
source_text: LXXVIII. Hoc praesertim videre est in judicio Theologorum Nassovio-Wateravicorum circa tertium & quartum articulum, quod habetur in actis Synodi Dordracenae. Ibi enim explicantes suam Thesin de intentione Dei in hominis vocatione, dicunt gratiam praedicationis & illuminationis, quae hypocritis cum piis communis est, ad conversionem secundum quid sufficientem esse, hoc est, in ordine causarum secundarum, seu mediorum; quatenus nulla alia conversionis media, sive externae praedicationis, sive internae illuminationis, praeter illa requiruntur: Sed non esse sufficientem ad conversionem simpliciter, hoc est, sine internae tractionis gratia; sine qua quenquam converti & ad Christum venire Scriptura pronunciat impossibile.
pass_a_gloss: LXXVIII. This may be seen especially in the judgment of the Nassau-Wetterau Theologians on the third & fourth article, which is found in the acts of the Synod of Dort. For there, explaining their Thesis on the intention of God in the calling of man, they say that the grace of preaching & illumination, which is common to hypocrites with the godly, is sufficient for conversion in a certain respect, that is, in the order of second causes, or of means; inasmuch as no other means of conversion, whether of external preaching, or of internal illumination, are required besides those: But that it is not sufficient for conversion absolutely, that is, without the grace of internal drawing; without which Scripture pronounces it impossible that anyone be converted & come to Christ.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXVIII. A clear case is the Nassau-Wetterau theologians' judgment on the third and fourth articles, preserved in the Acts of the Synod of Dort. In setting out their thesis on what God intends when he calls people, they grant that preaching and enlightenment, a grace hypocrites have in common with the godly, suffices for conversion in one respect: at the level of secondary causes or means, in that conversion requires no further means beyond these, whether of outward preaching or of inward enlightenment.

Taken without qualification, though, it does not suffice, that is, without the grace of being drawn from within; and without that grace, Scripture declares, it is impossible for anyone to be converted and come to Christ.
